description_full: Yalla Group Limited, together with its subsidiaries, operates a social networking and gaming platform in the Middle East and North Africa region. It offers mobile applications, including Yalla, a voice-centric group chat platform; and Yalla Ludo, a casual gaming application. The company's platform provides group chatting and games services; and consume virtual currencies to purchase virtual items, as well as provides upgrade services. It has operations in United Arab Emirates, Mainland China, Hongkong, Cayman Islands, Saudia Arabia, and Singapore countries. The company was formerly known as FYXTech Corporation. Yalla Group Limited was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates.

Each employee generates $160K of free cash flow annually. Stock-based compensation of $12K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: Yalla Group Limited is a small-cap technology business with a $837M market cap on $342M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +6.6pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 79% against a 10% cost of capital — a 69-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $136M in free cash flow — roughly 40 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.93× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 6.8% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 34% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
